nodes.label: The post-login callback Location gains a trailing slash while the session cookie Path is left bare
nodes.norm_label: post-login callback location slashed while cookie path left bare
nodes.description: apps/learn/src/pages/api/auth/callback.ts returns a 302 whose Location was changed from "/fasttrack/dashboard" to "/fasttrack/dashboard/" while the adjacent Set-Cookie in the same header block still reads Path=/fasttrack/dashboard. The diff is one insertion and one deletion; the report states the cookie Path and the comments were deliberately left untouched.

nodes.label: ashpd CreateSessionOptions exposes no app_id
nodes.norm_label: ashpd create session options exposes no app id
nodes.description: Reused id, same claim. ashpd is pinned at 0.13.13 (Cargo.lock:250-251, resolved by apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:119) and ashpd-0.13.13/src/desktop/session.rs:164-171 shows CreateSessionOptions as a struct of two pub(crate) HandleToken fields with no app_id, no public constructor and no builder.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t2-explicit-portal-app-id [ses_f1d2226bdffeez05xKmOV1sY4W].md:L5933] "There is no public seam through which `app_id` could be supplied, so the \"pure function that builds the session options\" the brief asked for cannot exist against this crate version." The note's own reason, not the one chunk-rem-007 recorded.

nodes.label: The portal frontend forwards only whitelisted CreateSession option keys, so a client-added app_id is silently dropped
nodes.norm_label: portal frontend filters session options to a two key whitelist
nodes.description: xdg-desktop-portal/desktop-portal/global-shortcuts.c:214-217 and :245-252 pass the client options vardict through xdp_filter_options (shared/xdp-utils.c:294-337), which copies only the two whitelisted keys into the forwarded dict. The backend call at global-shortcuts.c:289 supplies app_id from xdp_app_info_get_id(request->app_info), so the key is never read from the client on any path. Narrower than the ashpd claim: it holds even for a client that could send the key at all.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t2-explicit-portal-app-id [ses_f1d2226bdffeez05xKmOV1sY4W].md:L5945] "`xdp_filter_options` (`shared/xdp-utils.c:294-337`) copies only whitelisted keys into the forwarded dict, so a client-added `app_id` would be silently dropped and never reach the backend."

nodes.label: Portal identity derived from process cgroup
nodes.norm_label: portal identity derived from process cgroup
nodes.description: Reused id, same claim, now pinned to the host-side implementation. For an unsandboxed host process xdp_app_info_get_id resolves to sd_pid_get_user_unit(pid) plus a unit-name regex (shared/xdp-app-info-host.c:150-187 and :100-146), reading the process cgroup. Confirmed read-only on this host: konsole runs in app-org.kde.konsole-1262.scope and a child inherits it; a desktop-entry launch is instantiated by the app-*.service template, which regex2 resolves to snipset-desktop.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t2-explicit-portal-app-id [ses_f1d2226bdffeez05xKmOV1sY4W].md:L5949] "It reads the process's cgroup, and the identity is a property of the launch context, not of anything the app can pass." The note's own follow-on reason, [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t2-explicit-portal-app-id [ses_f1d2226bdffeez05xKmOV1sY4W].md:L5958] "All 31 misattributed episodes in T1 are this, and the named string at `mod.rs:700` is a symptom, not a cause."

nodes.label: AppID::from_str requires at least two dot-separated segments, so a bare snipset-desktop is rejected as an AppID
nodes.norm_label: appid from str requires two dot separated segments
nodes.description: ashpd app_id.rs:218-223 rejects a single-segment string in AppID::from_str, so the plan's chosen identity "snipset-desktop" is not a valid AppID and survives only as the MaybeAppID fallback string (app_id.rs:97-104). This is a second, independent failure of the plan's identity string, separate from there being no app_id field to put it in.

nodes.label: Refusing a look-alike patch that reads as a fix but never reaches the wire, and halting the task instead
nodes.norm_label: refuse a lookalike impl that never reaches the wire
nodes.description: The whole T2 outcome. Having established that the brief's proven root cause does not survive verification, the subagent wrote zero files, classified the result as `contract`, exit 0, E_PRECOND_DEP, and returned three costed options instead of choosing one. Its stated principle is that a fake field or string-insertion shim is worse than no change.

Worse than no change, because it would read as a fix and T5's live check would \"pass\" on a code change that never reached the wire." The task then halted at [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t2-explicit-portal-app-id [ses_f1d2226bdffeez05xKmOV1sY4W].md:L5918] "## T2: halted at a precondition failure. Zero files changed." rather than proceeding.

nodes.label: xsel serves a hard-coded fixed atom list and cannot offer a custom target, so it is excluded from the file-attachment path
nodes.norm_label: xsel serves a hard coded fixed atom list and cannot offer a custom target
nodes.description: Verified from the man page and from source. kfish/xsel master xsel.c compiles a fixed supported_targets array under MAX_NUM_TARGETS 9, filled in main() with TIMESTAMP, MULTIPLE, TARGETS, DELETE, INCR, TEXT, UTF8_STRING and XA_STRING; handle_targets() serves that array verbatim and the SelectionRequest handler sets property None for anything else. The man page has no target-atom flag at all, and its -t means --selectionTimeout, not a MIME type.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h09-external-cli-mime-flags [ses_f08b3c99dffezYuPHkDgPcrL2B].md:L4399] "Verdict: `xsel` must be excluded from the file-attachment path. This is not a limitation of the documentation; it is a hard-coded limit in the program." The trap is named at L4406 and the consequence at L4451: xsel can only put a file:// string in as UTF8_STRING/STRING text, which every consumer treats as a literal string to paste rather than a file reference.

nodes.label: wl-copy and xclip each hold a single target, so a text/uri-list plus UTF8_STRING combination is impossible from a shell pipeline
nodes.norm_label: wl-copy and xclip can each offer only one mime type
nodes.description: wl-copy's man page BUGS section states there is no way to copy data in multiple MIME types, tracked as bugevaevc/wl-clipboard issue #71, which the note retrieved directly and found Open since 13 Oct 2019 with label enhancement and no assignee. xclip's xclip.c holds a single global scalar `Atom target` (default XA_STRING) set through doOptTarget, not an array. Both therefore advertise exactly one type, and both are usable for text/uri-list but neither can add a text/plain companion.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h09-external-cli-mime-flags [ses_f08b3c99dffezYuPHkDgPcrL2B].md:L4641] "You cannot do it with `wl-copy` or `xclip`. Both hold a single target" ... "This is a tool limitation, not a platform requirement — nothing in GTK, Qt, or KIO source requires a `text/plain` companion." The note attributes the fix, if one is ever wanted, to a native client using `wl_data_source.offer` several times, not to a shell pipeline.

nodes.label: xclip defaults to XA_PRIMARY, so -selection clipboard must be passed explicitly
nodes.norm_label: xclip default selection is primary not clipboard
nodes.description: Verified from the xclip man page. -selection accepts primary, secondary and clipboard, and the default is XA_PRIMARY, the mouse-selection buffer. The man page also notes only the first character matters, so -selection c is legal, though the full word is what should be written.

nodes.label: A text/uri-list payload is CRLF-terminated, one URI per line, percent-encoded, with no comment lines and no trailing newline
nodes.norm_label: text uri list payload needs crlf and percent encoding
nodes.description: Narrower than the general choice of text/uri-list as the file-reference format. IANA's registration of text/uri-list (RFC 2483) states the format: lines beginning with # are comments, each URI on one and only one line, and all text/* lines terminated with CRLF. Reader behaviour was checked in Qt 6 qmimedata.cpp dataToUrls(), which splits on \n only, trims the \r, and skips empty lines, and the note flags that Qt does not skip # comment lines as GTK, Chromium and the RFC do. Local files are file:/// with three slashes and no authority, built with g_filename_to_uri or QUrl::fromLocalFile().toString(QUrl::FullyEncoded) rather than by hand.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h09-external-cli-mime-flags [ses_f08b3c99dffezYuPHkDgPcrL2B].md:L4531] "**Recommendation:** emit **CRLF** (spec-correct, and both verified readers tolerate it), **no `#` comment lines** (Qt does not skip them ...), **no trailing newline** (avoids an empty final line; harmless in Qt but unspecified elsewhere), **percent-encode** the path." The normative CRLF sentence is quoted from the registration at L4479.

nodes.label: GTK decides a paste is a file by inspecting the TARGETS atom
nodes.norm_label: gtk decides a paste is a file by inspecting the targets atom
nodes.description: Reused id, same claim, now sourced from GTK 3.24.49 gtk/gtkclipboard.c where gtk_clipboard_request_uris() hard-codes the atom name gdk_atom_intern_static_string("text/uri-list"), corroborated by the GTK 3 Clipboard class documentation for gtk_clipboard_wait_for_uris and gtk_clipboard_wait_is_uris_available.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h09-external-cli-mime-flags [ses_f08b3c99dffezYuPHkDgPcrL2B].md:L4556] "GTK decides whether to offer \"Paste\" for a file by inspecting the TARGETS atom. Your producer must answer TARGETS with text/uri-list in it, or GTK will never request it." The note adds the producer-side mirror check: wl-copy's -l, --list-types.

nodes.label: application/x-kde-cutselection is only the cut-vs-copy flag and is not required for a file attachment to paste as an attachment
nodes.norm_label: x kde cutselection is not needed to deliver an attachment
nodes.description: Verified from KDE/kio src/widgets/paste.cpp. KIO::setClipboardDataCut writes a single ASCII byte, "1" for cut and "0" for copy, and carries no file list; KIO::pasteActionText builds its "Paste One File" / "Paste N Items" entries from KUrlMimeData::urlsFromMimeData(mimeData) alone, so the paste action is gated on the URI list with no cutselection present. extractFormats() in the same file skips application/x-kde-* when enumerating paste formats. Qt's QMimeData::hasUrls/urls/setUrls map to text/uri-list per the Qt 6 documentation.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h09-external-cli-mime-flags [ses_f08b3c99dffezYuPHkDgPcrL2B].md:L4629] "It carries one ASCII byte, `\"1\"` = cut, `\"0\"` = copy. It carries no file list. So: you do not need it to deliver an attachment. You would need it only to make Ctrl+X-style move semantics available." The gating line is at L4611.
